architecture_decisions:
:
- **Canonical durable PLAN versus candidate-local selection `primary_plan` is the exact protected PLAN accepted for the Engineering Run and remains the authoritative worker-checkpoint plan for the duration of that IMPLEMENT attempt. A candidate-local alternate plan is subordinate selection evidence only: it may alter the already-admitted selected producer set for one disposable candidate, but it is not a PLAN transition and cannot replace the worker checkpoint `plan_ref`. Proposal generation therefore carries two explicit inputs when they differ: 1. candidate-local orchestration plan — used for scheduling, task binding, assignment identity, producer identity, and candidate strategy/evaluation evidence; 2. canonical durable plan — used only for worker checkpoint PLAN identity and the protected compatibility check. For the primary candidate both inputs are the same object/identity.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — The workstream records exact production/QA evidence that P2-V0.23.32 reached `candidate-repair / PROPOSAL_ASSEMBLY / AGENTIC_CONTRACT_ERROR` after primary candidate proposal completion, with no evidence of an additional repair hosted call, satisfying #543's later-bounded-blocker alternative without claiming end-to-end success.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Candidate proposal generation receives the canonical durable `primary_plan` separately from any candidate-local plan, and the primary candidate behavior remains identical when both are the same plan.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Tests prove a candidate-local plan with changed Project/run/Work Specification/acceptance/policy/work-graph identity is rejected before hosted generation or durable checkpoint mutation; roster/selected-producer variation already admitted by candidate selection remains allowed.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — A deterministic live/resilient regression reproduces primary validation rejection followed by candidate-repair and proves all worker checkpoints retain exactly `agentic-plan:{primary_plan.plan_id}`.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — The same regression proves candidate-repair uses a distinct candidate-local producer/assignment/task/operation/request/attempt identity from the primary round; no round-1 task identity or cached request is reused as the repair dispatch.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Repair eligibility remains limited to the P2-V0.23.32 fixed static-web BUILD/TEST/VERIFY reasons, uses the same immutable execution contract and authoritative base source, and a replacement validation failure remains terminal with no third candidate.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Tests prove maximum candidate rounds, per-work-unit recovery, final validator repair, hosted timeout, zero hidden provider retries, and Luna/Terra/Sol admission are unchanged.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — A successful repair still passes exact proposal/acceptance validation, SafeImplementationEngine, real disposable BUILD/TEST/VERIFY, independent evaluation/routing, and selected-candidate checks before canonical IMPLEMENT acceptance.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Tests prove any candidate/canonical plan incompatibility is represented only by closed server-owned evidence and cannot persist exception text, source/generated content, raw validator/provider output, credentials, environment values, filesystem roots, or true authority claims.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — SpecCritic/SpecCompiler evidence for this exact spec, focused regressions, full API regression, applicable client checks, protected promotion evaluation, Bounded Autonomy, Workstream Spec Validation, and exact-head PR gates are green.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — After exact merged API source reaches READY with production canary, `/health` and `/ready` are HTTP 200, and runtime scan is clean, retry the equivalent marker-free authenticated path. It must invoke the repair hosted generation without changing canonical worker `plan_ref` and then advance canonical IMPLEMENT or expose a genuinely later bounded blocker. Repeating `candidate-repair / PROPOSAL_ASSEMBLY` due plan identity does not pass.

critique: The protected `primary_plan` accepted for the Engineering Run remains the only durable PLAN identity for worker checkpoints during an IMPLEMENT attempt. Candidate-local challenger/repair plans remain non-authoritative server-owned producer-selection evidence. They may select only already-admitted agents and may not become a durable PLAN replacement. Candidate-local plans may share a canonical worker PLAN checkpoint only when Project ID, run ID, Work Specification ID/revision/digest, exact acceptance contract, agent-protocol version, policy identity, and work-graph identity are compatible with the canonical `primary_plan`. Roster/selected-producer identity may differ only inside the existing bounded candidate-selection contract. Worker checkpoint `plan_ref` must remain `agentic-plan:{primary_plan.plan_id}` across candidate-primary, candidate-repair, and any existing bounded challenger round. No candidate round can authorize a PLAN-ref change. Candidate scheduling, AgentTaskRequest creation, producer attribution, and unique assignment/operation/request/attempt identity continue to use the candidate-local plan. This prevents repair from replaying round-1 dispatch identity…
